evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'Who to tell, in what order, and what each one needs.' plus sub 'Settle is a checklist for adult children settling a parent's affairs in England and Wales...' names what, who and where in two lines; the action 'Copy my checklist' has a stated object ('copies your list as plain text'). Nothing later contradicts it.
evidence.fit: Not-legal-advice and England-and-Wales-only appear inside the artifact's example line in the first screen and get a full section ('It covers England and Wales, and it is not legal advice'). Tone is calm and practical, no urgency or selling. The 'nowhere to send sign-ups' constraint is handled literally: the interest form says 'Nothing is sent. It stays on this page, in this browser.' Weak spot: the hero says 'Nothing to sign up for' while the bottom section invites an email, and a browser-only email save does not really collect interest for the client.
evidence.distinctiveness: The 'tick what they had, the list puts itself in order' chip grid with numbered lines, 'Have ready' document tags and italic 'letter' markers comes directly from the product; the document 'kit' cards with dotted fill-in fields and the 'Comes later' stamp on Grant of probate are product-specific. The frame around them (two-column hero, three-card row, split letter section, two-column scope, form card) is a familiar SaaS skeleton, and Lora+Inter is a common pairing.
evidence.proof: The working checklist sits in the right column of the 1440 first screen and directly under the CTA at 768/390. Operated at 1440/768/390: ticking 'A car' went 11->13 contacts and 6->8 letters, inserting 'Their car insurer' and 'DVLA, about the car' highlighted in yellow; ticking Rented and unticking Owned/A will swapped in 'Their landlord or housing association' and changed 'Read the will' to 'Check for a will'. Labelled 'Example:' at the top of the artifact. Numbers in the summary match the rendered list in every state I tried.
evidence.craft: Clear hierarchy: serif display H1, white sheet artifact on a grey-green ground, consistent row rhythm in the list, selected chips get tint+border+tick. No overlaps or clipping at 1440/768/390 in any state; axe clean. Minor: 'Have ready' labels and document tags are 13px and low-emphasis grey; the 1440 hero's left column leaves a large empty area under the CTA beside the long list (sticky lede helps when scrolling); fonts are named but not embedded, so Lora/Inter fall back to Georgia/Helvetica on most devices.
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, sub and full-width-feeling 'Copy my checklist' button in the first viewport, the artifact heading starts at ~y 535 and chips at ~y 760, so the artifact begins but is not usable without one scroll. Chips are 2-up, 44px+ tall, labels wrap to two lines ('Owned their / home'). Nav stays as three 44px links on a second row, no hamburger needed. Copy feedback 'Copied. 11 lines are on your clipboard' appears right under the button. The 11-line list becomes a long column (~1900px) before anything else; no overflow at 390 or 320.
evidence.honesty: 'Example:' label is at the top of the artifact; the CTA states what it does before the click ('It copies your list as plain text'); the interest form says 'Nothing is sent' before submitting and 'Saved in this browser only. Nothing has been sent, because there is nowhere to send it yet.' after. Sample letter is labelled 'Sample letter, written for this page'. No invented proof.
evidence.interaction: All 8 chips toggle by click; summary updates with correct singular/plural ('1 wants... 0 come'); 'Start again' restores the example defaults; new lines flash a fading highlight; both 'Copy my checklist' buttons report success beside the button (clipboard fallback textarea exists in code). Nav anchors scroll to sections. Form: empty -> 'Type an email address first. Nothing was saved.'; 'nope' -> 'That does not look like an email address. Nothing was saved.'; valid -> saved message. No console errors at any width.
evidence.copy: Specific, plain and kind: 'Redirecting the post to you catches the accounts nobody knew about', 'you do not write the sentence about your parent's death over and over', 'A call with the right one in front of you is one call, not three.' Buttons say what happens ('Save my request here'). Slight instruction-manual cadence in places ('Tick what they had' is brisk for a grieving reader) and the 'Nothing to sign up for' / email form contradiction.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience in the sub, the live example checklist with 'Example:' label and an action whose label matches what it does, all in one viewport. 390: promise, audience and action are in view but only the artifact's heading and example label, not the chips or the list, so the believability shown at 1440 drops on the phone.

problems: The client wants to collect interest, but the only interest path saves the email in the visitor's own browser and the hero says 'Nothing to sign up for', so the page collects nothing and contradicts itself.
At 390 the artifact starts at the bottom of the first screen and the 11-line list becomes a ~1900px column before the next idea; no grouping by week as the list grows.
Generic outer skeleton (two-column hero, three-card row, split sections) and unembedded Lora/Inter make the frame feel templated around a strong artifact; 13px grey 'Have ready' tags are faint.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Everyone you need to tell, in the order to tell them.' with lede 'After a parent dies... Settle is a checklist that takes it one contact at a time' makes what and who clear at 1440 and 390; next step is deferred to 'a place to leave your email at the bottom of this page' with no control in view.
evidence.fit: Tone is the best fit for this reader: quiet single-column serif, 'Nothing ticked yet. That's fine.', 'If you're reading this in the first weeks, there's no hurry.' Not-legal-advice and England/Wales are in a tinted box in the first screen. But the brief says there is nowhere to send sign-ups, and the page's main action pretends otherwise: the form keeps the email in localStorage and replies 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' A stated constraint is not reflected in what the page does.
evidence.distinctiveness: Feels like a considerate letter rather than a startup page: TeX Gyre Schola embedded, 36rem measure, italic 'England and Wales' in the header, manila letter block. But structurally it is a plain essay column with a checklist, a sample card and an is/isn't list; there is no visual idea beyond typography, and at 1440 the narrow column leaves ~450px empty either side.
evidence.proof: The checklist is real content (8 items in two time groups with when/how lines) and the bank contact page with 'What they'll ask for', 'What happens next' and a manila letter is strong proof. But it starts below the 1440 first screen (H2 at ~y 755, first checkbox ~y 1000), is a fixed list where ticking only greys items out, and does not show the 'right order for your situation' that the promise implies. The contact page is introduced as 'a page like this' rather than an explicit 'Example' label on the card.
evidence.craft: Deliberate type scale and generous rhythm; ticks animate a stroke, ticked items grey and collapse their 'how' text; muted colour palette passes axe. No defects at 1440/768/390 in states operated. Minor: header wordmark link 32px tall, inline links 22-26px; 1440 first screen is all text with large side margins and no visual anchor.
evidence.mobile: 390: the page was essentially designed for the phone; H1, lede, 'isn't ready yet' line and disclaimer fill the first screen, the checklist starts at ~y 790. Checkbox rows are full-width labels well over 44px; tick state persisted after reload ('2 of 8 done.'). Email field and button stack full-width. No overflow at 390/320. But no action control is in the first screens, and the sign-up sits ~4000px down.
evidence.honesty: Sign-up success is false: entering jo@example.co.uk and pressing 'Tell me when it's ready' shows 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' while the script only pushes the address into localStorage['settle-interest'] (SIGNUP_ENDPOINT = ''). Nothing before the click says it is not sent; the intro says 'Leave your email and we'll send one message when Settle opens'. Elsewhere honest: 'It isn't ready yet' in the hero, legal disclaimer prominent, ticks 'saved on your device and go nowhere else'.
evidence.interaction: Checkboxes work by click and keyboard (Space on focused #c2 ticked it), tally updates ('2 of 8 done.', 'All 8 done. Everything else can wait a while.'), 'Clear the ticks' resets, state survives reload. Form shows 'That doesn't look like an email address. Could you check it?' for empty and invalid input. The success state reports something that did not happen, and the checklist does not respond to the visitor's situation.
evidence.copy: Warm, specific, well-judged for grief: 'After a parent dies, the paperwork arrives all at once.', 'Keep the heating ticking over if the house is empty in winter.', 'Scotland and Northern Ireland have different rules, and we'd rather not guess at them.' Marked down because the sign-up copy ('we'll send one message when Settle opens', 'We'll write once') promises something the page cannot do.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 and 390: a specific promise and an honest 'It isn't ready yet' with the legal box, but no artifact or example in view and no action control, only a pointer to the bottom of the page; the action it points to does not do what it says.

problems: The sign-up reports 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' but the email is only stored in the visitor's browser; the brief says there is nowhere to send sign-ups, and the page says nothing about that before or after the click.
The first screen has no artifact and no action at either width; the checklist starts below the fold at 1440 and the only action is ~4000px down.

The checklist is a fixed list that only greys items out, so it does not show the product's ordering doing work for the visitor's situation; at 1440 the narrow column leaves the first screen text-only with wide empty margins.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The sign-up is the page's only conversion action (the first screen points to it: 'there's a place to leave your email at the bottom of this page'). Submitting a valid email shows 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' but nothing is sent anywhere: SIGNUP_ENDPOINT is '' so the script only writes the address to localStorage['settle-interest'] in the visitor's browser. No text before the click says it will not be sent; the intro says 'Leave your email and we'll send one message when Settle opens'. This reports success for something that did not happen.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/B/index.html from disk at 390x844. Scroll to 'If you'd like to know when it's ready'. Type jo@example.co.uk, tap 'Tell me when it's ready'. The green box reads 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' In DevTools run localStorage.getItem('settle-interest') to see the email stored locally; check the script (SIGNUP_ENDPOINT = '') and Network panel: no request is made.

reason: A puts a working, labelled example of the product's core job (the list re-ordering itself from what the parent had) in the first screen and is honest at every action, including saying the email goes nowhere yet. B has the more fitting typography and voice for a grieving reader, but its first screen has no artifact or action and its only conversion step falsely tells the visitor 'We'll write once'. If B's form said up front that nothing is sent yet and the checklist appeared higher, the gap would narrow a lot; tone alone would not flip it.
